text:
ria: Heads-up — customer reported inconsistent audit events in Console export and a 403 when attempting export. This started after the audit_events schema migration last week. Can we quick sync?

audit-bot: migration audit_events_v2 deployed to prod @ 1713960000. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/audit-schema-migration (migration job ran with --dry-run=false).

noah (product): Important — the Console viewer also paginates weirdly for long ranges. Customers want cursor-based server-side pagination for exports so they can stream >30 days. Is that on the backlog?

alex (frontend): I saw two issues: our viewer flattens nested JSON and the CSV exporter drops nested maps entirely. Current flattening uses `flattenForCsv(obj, {separator: '_'})` which loses arrays/objects. Also UI was checking `user.role === 'admin'` client-side only — backend endpoint does an RBAC check but the new RBAC v2 split may have left some orgs without `audit:export`.

maria (support): Report from Acme Corp: tried to export 90 days, got 403. Their org admin shows as "Org Admin" but not allowed to export. They escalated to legal for audit. Need a workaround asap.

ria: Quick notes from infra/security: RBAC v2 introduced scoped permissions and we split `admin` into `org:admin` and `org:billing` etc. During migration we intended to backfill `audit:export` for role=org:admin but looks like that backfill job failed for some tenants. KMS integration affects envelope encryption of event payloads (logs at rest) but not the export permission logic.

chris (sec-eng): Triage plan: 1) Reproduce with customer org id; 2) Check migration logs for backfill failures (look for key `backfill_audit_export`). 3) Compare schema diffs — IIRC fields renamed `actor_id` -> `principal_id` and `target` -> `resource` which could break post-processing/validators used by exporter. 4) Add a graceful transformer in the export service to accept both names for 48h while we backfill DB.

alex (frontend): UX/engineering proposal: - add server-side cursor pagination + streaming endpoint for export. - CSV export should include a single `raw_event_json` column with full JSON and a best-effort flattened set of common columns (timestamp, principal, action, resource). - disable client-only role checks; show export button only when backend returns `can_export: true`. - export endpoints require scope `audit:export` enforced in middleware.

noah (product): Who owns the customer comms and ETA? We need a short customer-facing note and an ETA for the fix so support can respond.

ria: I'll own the triage and backfill job. Plan: re-run backfill for missing orgs and launch a small migration patch within 48h. Chris — can you prepare the transformer patch and validator relax (accept both `actor_id` and `principal_id`)? Alex — can you gate the export UI and add the `raw_event_json` column so CSV won't lose payloads?

chris (sec-eng): Yep, will ship a quick validator patch and unit tests today; will add transformer in export pipeline.

alex (frontend): I'll put a hotfix behind a feature flag for gating + add the CSV change. Need API change: `GET /v1/audit/permissions?org_id=...` -> returns `{can_export: true, can_view: true}` (backend will be the source of truth).

maria (support): Interim workaround to send to Acme: run export via API with an org-admin token and `include_raw=true`. Example curl (replace TOKEN and ORG):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?org_id=ORG123&start=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-31T23:59:59Z&include_raw=true" \
  -o acme_audit_202603.jsonl
```
Explain we will backfill permissions and upload a fixed CSV if needed.

noah (product): Good — please draft an external note: short incident description, affected customers, workaround, ETA to fix (~48h), and contact for follow-up. I'll review.

ria: Will post the draft in #incidents and assign an owner for the external comms. Also adding a short-term monitoring alert for `audit.export.failed` and `migration.backfill.failed`.

maria (support): Thanks — I'll send the workaround and keep the ticket updated. If legal pushes, loop me in. :thumbsup:

alex (frontend): One more thought — pagination cursors should be opaque server-generated cursors referencing snapshot id so downstream schema changes don't break paging. Adding that to the design doc.

ria: Great. Re-running backfill now and will post status in this thread.

(--- thread will be updated with backfill logs ---)
